scope: First reconnect component: each physical browser client captures enrolled actor/device/signing/server-signature trust values before its first await. Component proof uses bounded Node WebSocket fixtures with actual WebCrypto signatures; no TLS/network/installed-browser/reconnect-matrix qualification.
behavior: A caller may prepare a new physical peer by editing its construction draft. Those edits cannot change an existing or still-opening peer identity, device metadata, signing identity or server-signature trust. Required properties are captured through property lookup, including inherited values. CryptoKey handles and caller AbortSignal remain their intended immutable-key/live-cancellation references. No mutation is replayed or new transport automatically selected.

negative.scope: Both signing algorithms: pending-open actor/device draft edits and authenticated-peer server trust edits expose original reference adoption.

intermediate_candidate.disposition: Own-property-only copying dropped inherited enrollment fields. Final code explicitly captures required properties without changing the public option interface.

remaining: Preferred transport, selected path and fallback reason with bounded physical selection.
Fresh credential/trust resolution and current authorization after reconnect; no fallback on authentication/trust/protocol refusals.
Original operation references/status and cursor snapshot recovery without mutation resend.
Dropped acknowledgments, actual WSS/WT outages, expired credentials and repeated reconnect mid-consult/handoff.
Distinguish transport migration, media reconnection and explicit device replacement; no uninterrupted media promise after server crash.
